Odin × Godot

Gate C authoring/export validation

4 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Normal export preset setupReproduced build limits

Gate C covers actual exported Host/Client runs of the same authored content through separate Kit and Replay adapters. A successful export and binary inspection are prerequisites, not runtime acceptance. Current work keeps each framework/target result separate in the final report.

All four required cases passed. The Gate C report binds each normal export to its actual exported Host/Client run, raw logs, complete five-part bytes, remote controls, loaded Native image and measured cleanup. These are target120 functional checks; production hardening remains in Phase 6.

Required case Execution scope Acceptance evidence
Kit / macOS arm64 Native arm64 SDK and Native modules; official universal Godot launcher PASS: export, inspection, exported pair
Replay / macOS arm64 Same architecture boundary PASS: separate export and exported pair
Kit / Linux x86-64 ELF64 x86-64 userspace translated by Rosetta on the available Linux arm64 VM PASS: Native matrix, export, exported pair
Replay / Linux x86-64 Same translated functional scope PASS: separate export and exported pair

Translated Linux execution is not native x86 hardware performance evidence. The universal macOS launcher is not a claim that arm64-only SDK modules support Intel. No cross-target deterministic equality is inferred by comparing separate same-build Host/Client cases. Existing simulation/profile bounds and ownership contracts remain unchanged.

Normal export preset setup#

The two authored examples provide the same exact preset names: macOS arm64 (macOS, Godot launcher selector universal, ARM64 SDK/runtime scope) and Linux x86_64 (Linux, architecture x86_64). macOS declares minimum11.0, unique org.odingodot.box3d.kitauthoring and org.odingodot.box3d.replayauthoring bundle identifiers, Godot built-in ad-hoc signing and notarization disabled. These are local test bundles, not signed release/notarized/uploaded distribution. Actual bundle architecture/minimumOS and library loading still require inspection of the exported files.

The matching official macOS template contains only the normal universal Godot launcher. It is exported unchanged through the ordinary exporter: no custom PCK/template patch or lipo thinning. The preset display name macOS arm64 denotes the SDK Core/scripts/modules/shared Native consumers and actual test execution, which remain ARM64. Export inspection requires the launcher's actual architecture list to contain ARM64 and records that list, while every SDK/Native consumer must still be ARM64. This does not claim a universal SDK, Intel execution or Intel compatibility. Actual binary inspection/runtime evidence, not the preset label, establishes those facts.

Use examples/box3d_authoring_shared/prepare.py in a NEW task output with the correct target's explicit verified shared Native library/SHA. It already copies export_presets.cfg unchanged with the ordinary project; no special staging or packer is added. Build the standard SDK Core/scripts/modules, import with the matching official Godot/templates, then invoke the normal exporter, for example:

Shell
python3 examples/box3d_authoring_shared/prepare.py --framework kit \
  --out "$WORK/kit" --native-library "$NATIVE" --native-sha256 "$NATIVE_SHA" \
  --odin "$ODIN" --godot "$GODOT" --build
# Exporter's ordinary optimized build subprocess also needs the selected SDK/Native.
export ROOT="$SDK_ROOT" ODIN_GODOT_ROOT="$SDK_ROOT" BOX3D_NATIVE_LIBRARY="$NATIVE"
"$GODOT" --headless --editor --path "$WORK/kit/project" --quit-after 120
"$GODOT" --headless --path "$WORK/kit/project" \
  --export-release "macOS arm64" "$WORK/exports/KitBox3DAuthoring.app"

Use --framework replay/ReplayBox3DAuthoring.app for Replay. Linux uses its verified Linux x86_64 shared .so, the same ordinary plugin/build flow and --export-release "Linux x86_64" .../kit-box3d-authoring.x86_64 (or Replay). Do not use a macOS library in the Linux export. ODIN must identify the intended target-capable compiler; export flags/target selection belong to the ordinary SDK export plugin, not per-scene glue. Keep all output PCK/shared objects/modules and adjacent metadata together. No manual PCK or ODIN_SCRIPTS_DLL override is part of exported execution.

Both presets use all_resources plus explicit normal .odin, GDScript, .tres, .tscn, .gdextension, JSON/config inclusion, so helper/module sources and authored resources remain available to the supported export pipeline. Native and module deployment remains the normal GDExtension/Odin export-plugin job; there is no static engine duplication. The configuration-only reader tests/box3d_gate_c/presets/validate.py checks names/arch/signing/source-inclusion and identical shared content, without running Godot. Its result is not an export or runtime pass.

Root/p/q own actual platform exports, file/loader inspection and record creation. A record marked PASS means actual export and file inspection only; Root's separate exported Host/Client controller must still prove state/inputs/final ACK, natural cleanup and one Native image. Linux Rosetta execution is translated functional evidence, not native x86 performance or cross-target determinism. Final Gate C classification and its report remain Root-owned.

Reproduced build limits#

The original Linux task container reached its 1536 MiB limit and recorded two OOM kills while Godot invoked Odin during export. One compiler thread alone did not resolve the failed exports. The passing setup used a 6144 MiB VM, a 4096 MiB task container and export-only SCRIPT_BUILD_FLAGS=-thread-count:1, retaining the normal -o:speed optimization. SDK and product memory limits were unchanged. Godot can return exit0 after reporting a failed script compilation, so the Linux harness also rejects error and leak messages in import/export logs.

The first Linux CTest supervisor stopped collecting a zombie test process. That attempt is retained as incomplete supervision, without a product verdict. The replacement queried the actual CTest registration and ran every registered command with the same arguments, working directory, properties and dependency order, using file logs and direct waits. All 12 commands passed in Debug and Release, including another complete run after the memory change. These records explicitly say actual_ctest_run_pass:false. The SDK profile verifies their source/binary identity, registration and logs rather than inventing a CTest PASS.

The report preserves failed attempts and the controlled VM resource change. Only two idle containers belonging to this goal were stopped and restored; user container states and the default connection were preserved. The recorded rollback is for safe goal cleanup after checking for newly active user work.
